newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia in the middle of job slump - oppn.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia in the middle of job slump - oppn.

text.p: Australian opposition employment spokesman Martin Ferguson said on Thursday the country was in a job slump because of the government's emphasis on reducing the budget deficit.
"I say on behalf of the opposition that unfortunately we are in the middle of a major job slump," Ferguson told reporters.
"That's the problem for this government it has got an absolute budget deficit fetish without properly thinking through the medium term strategy and the consequences for unemployment," Ferguson said.
Although the budget deficit was in the process of being fixed, the problem for the government was that this would reduce the prospects of cutting unemployment, he said.
The seasonally adjusted unemployment rate rose to 8.8 percent in October from 8.7 percent in September, compared with 8.6 percent in October 1995, the Bureau of Statistics said.
The seasonally adjusted estimate of the number of employed persons rose 25,500 in October to 8.37 million, against 8.35 million in September and 8.24 million a year earlier.
